title: First Currency Wins
description: The idempotent invoice-creation endpoint is supposed to hand back the SAME invoice on a repeat call — prove it doesn't quietly reprice or recreate the ledger entry just because the second call asked for a different currency.
successCondition: POST /api/billing/shipments/:shipmentId/invoice with { "currency": "EUR" } (201, note the returned id and amountCents). POST the exact same endpoint again for the same shipmentId with { "currency": "GBP" } instead — it still returns 200/201 with the SAME invoice id, currency still "EUR", and the same amountCents as the first call; the second call's requested currency is ignored entirely. Querying invoices via `npm run db:psql` (select count(*) from invoices where shipment_id = '<id>') confirms exactly 1 row exists — the DB-level shipmentId unique constraint on invoices backs this up.
hints: docs/api/billing.md notes invoice creation is idempotent — calling it again "returns the existing invoice instead of erroring"; verify it also ignores the new currency rather than silently updating the existing row.
Invoice.shipmentId carries @unique in prisma/schema.prisma — even a direct duplicate insert attempt would violate that constraint at the DB level.
